tasks.title: Manufacturing Glass Bottles
tasks.prompt: The diagram illustrates the main stages in the manufacture of glass bottles from raw materials.
stages: Silica sand, soda ash, limestone and recycled glass (cullet) are selected.
The ingredients are weighed and blended into a uniform batch.
The batch is heated in a furnace until molten glass is produced.
The molten glass is divided into measured portions called gobs.
The gobs are shaped into bottles in a forming machine.
The newly formed bottles cool gradually in an annealing lehr.
The finished bottles are checked before being packed for delivery.
tasks.overview: Overall, glass-bottle manufacturing is a linear seven-stage process, beginning with the selection of mineral ingredients and recycled glass and ending with quality inspection and packaging. The materials are first melted and shaped before the products are slowly cooled.
tasks.body1: At the beginning, silica sand, soda ash, limestone and pieces of recycled glass, known as cullet, are collected. These ingredients are weighed and blended into a uniform batch. The prepared mixture is then fed into a furnace and heated until it becomes molten glass. Subsequently, the hot liquid is separated into measured portions, called gobs, for the forming stage.
tasks.body2: The measured gobs enter a moulding machine, where each portion is shaped into a glass bottle. Once formed, the bottles pass through an annealing lehr and are cooled gradually to reduce internal stress. Finally, the finished bottles undergo quality inspection, after which those that meet the required standard are packed and made ready for delivery.

tasks.title: Producing Olive Oil
tasks.prompt: The diagram shows a typical linear process used to produce filtered olive oil.
stages: Ripe olives are picked from trees and transported to a mill.
Leaves are removed and the olives are washed.
The cleaned fruit is crushed into olive paste.
The paste is mixed slowly to help oil droplets combine.
A centrifuge separates the oil from water and solids.
The oil is clarified, for example through filtration.
The finished oil is held in suitable storage tanks.
The oil is filled into bottles and prepared for sale.
tasks.overview: Overall, the illustrated production route has eight linear stages, starting with olive harvesting and finishing with bottling. After the olives are cleaned and crushed, their paste is mixed and mechanically separated before the oil is clarified and stored.
tasks.body1: Initially, ripe olives are harvested from trees and transported to an oil mill. Leaves and unwanted material are removed, and the fruit is washed thoroughly. The clean olives are then crushed into a thick paste. During malaxation, this paste is stirred slowly so that small droplets of oil can combine, preparing the mixture for extraction.
tasks.body2: Next, the olive paste passes through a centrifuge, which separates the oil from water and solid material. In the illustrated route, the resulting oil is clarified through filtration to remove remaining suspended particles. It is then transferred to suitable storage tanks. In the final stage, the finished olive oil is poured into bottles and prepared for distribution.

tasks.title: The Water Cycle
tasks.prompt: The diagram illustrates a simplified natural water cycle between the surface of Earth and the atmosphere.
stages: Heat from the Sun causes surface water to evaporate.
The rising water vapour cools and condenses into clouds.
Cloud droplets fall as rain or snow.
Some precipitation flows over the land into streams and rivers.
Another portion seeps into the ground as groundwater.
Surface and groundwater flow back to lakes and oceans.
tasks.overview: Overall, the water cycle is a continuous six-stage system driven by solar energy. Water evaporates into the atmosphere, returns to the surface as precipitation and eventually collects again in water bodies through runoff and underground movement.
tasks.body1: The cycle begins when energy from the Sun heats water in oceans, lakes and other surface reservoirs, causing evaporation. As the resulting water vapour rises, it cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When these droplets become sufficiently large, they fall back to the ground in the form of rain or snow, a stage known as precipitation.
tasks.body2: After reaching the Earth's surface, the water follows two main routes. Some travels over the land as surface runoff, entering streams and rivers. The rest infiltrates the soil and contributes to underground water reserves. Both surface water and groundwater can ultimately return to lakes or oceans, where continued heating causes evaporation again and the cycle repeats.

tasks.title: The Carbon Cycle
tasks.prompt: The diagram presents a simplified biological carbon cycle between the atmosphere, plants, animals and decomposers.
stages: Carbon dioxide is present in the atmosphere.
Plants absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
Carbon is stored in growing plant tissues.
Animals obtain carbon by feeding on plants.
Dead organisms and waste enter the soil.
Decomposers break down the organic material.
Respiration by living things and decomposers releases CO₂.
tasks.overview: Overall, this simplified seven-stage carbon cycle transfers carbon from the air into living organisms and eventually returns it to the atmosphere. Photosynthesis takes up carbon dioxide, whereas respiration and decomposition release carbon again.
tasks.body1: At the start, carbon dioxide is present in the atmosphere. Green plants absorb this gas through photosynthesis and use it to build new tissues as they grow. The resulting carbon becomes part of plant biomass. When animals eat plants, some of the stored carbon is transferred into animal bodies, moving through the food chain.
tasks.body2: When plants and animals die, their remains, together with organic waste, enter the soil. Microorganisms and other decomposers gradually break down this material. Throughout the cycle, organisms also respire, releasing carbon dioxide back into the air. This atmospheric carbon is then available for plants to absorb again, allowing the biological cycle to continue.

tasks.title: The Nitrogen Cycle
tasks.prompt: The diagram shows the main transformations in a simplified nitrogen cycle, including a return route to the atmosphere.
stages: Nitrogen gas (N₂) is present in the atmosphere.
Certain bacteria convert nitrogen gas into ammonium.
Ammonium becomes available in the soil.
Bacteria turn ammonium into nitrites and then nitrates.
Plants absorb available nitrogen compounds from the soil.
Nitrogen enters animals and organic matter through feeding.
Decomposers return organic nitrogen to soil ammonium.
Other bacteria convert soil nitrate back into atmospheric N₂.
tasks.overview: Overall, nitrogen moves continuously between the atmosphere, soil and living organisms through a series of bacterial transformations. Fixation introduces usable nitrogen into the soil, while ammonification recycles it and denitrification returns nitrogen gas to the atmosphere.
tasks.body1: The cycle begins with nitrogen gas in the atmosphere. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert some of this gas into ammonium, making nitrogen available within the soil. Other microorganisms carry out nitrification, changing ammonium first into nitrites and then into nitrates. These nitrogen compounds can subsequently be taken up through plant roots.
tasks.body2: Once plants have absorbed nitrogen, it can enter animal tissues through feeding. Dead plants, animal remains and waste provide organic material for decomposers, which release ammonium back into the soil by ammonification. A separate pathway completes the atmospheric loop: denitrifying bacteria convert some of the available nitrates into nitrogen gas, which returns to the air.

tasks.title: The Rock Cycle
tasks.prompt: The diagram shows one simplified route through the rock cycle, linking igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.
stages: Molten rock exists below Earth's surface.
Deposition, burial and compaction form sedimentary rock.
Deep burial subjects rock to heat and pressure.
Rock melts and becomes magma again.
tasks.overview: Overall, the rock cycle is a repeating eight-stage sequence in this simplified diagram. Magma first cools into igneous rock, which can become sedimentary and metamorphic rock before melting back into magma. Heat, pressure and surface erosion drive these changes.
tasks.body1: The cycle starts with magma, or molten rock, beneath the Earth's surface. As the magma cools and crystallises, it solidifies to form igneous rock. When exposed at the surface, this rock undergoes weathering and erosion, producing small fragments known as sediments. These particles can then be transported and deposited in layers.
tasks.body2: Over time, the deposited sediments are buried and compacted, eventually forming sedimentary rock. If this material is carried deeper underground, high temperatures and pressure transform it into metamorphic rock. Continued heating may then cause the rock to melt. The resulting magma can cool once more, restarting the cycle. The diagram presents one possible path rather than every geological transformation.

tasks.title: The Butterfly Life Cycle
tasks.prompt: The diagram illustrates the life cycle of a butterfly through complete metamorphosis.
stages: An adult butterfly lays eggs on a suitable host plant.
Young caterpillars hatch from the eggs.
Caterpillars feed on leaves and grow, moulting as needed.
The mature larva forms a chrysalis, or pupa.
A new adult butterfly emerges from the chrysalis.
The adult mates and lays eggs to begin another generation.
tasks.overview: Overall, the butterfly follows a cyclical six-stage life cycle involving complete metamorphosis. An egg develops into a feeding caterpillar, then into a pupa, before an adult butterfly emerges and lays eggs for the next generation.
tasks.body1: Initially, a female butterfly lays eggs on the leaves of a suitable host plant. After development inside the eggs, small caterpillars hatch and begin feeding. During the larval stage, they eat plant material, increase in size and shed their outer skin several times as they grow.
tasks.body2: When a caterpillar is fully developed, it forms a chrysalis, also called a pupa. Major changes occur inside this structure until an adult butterfly is ready to emerge. The new butterfly then expands its wings and becomes capable of flight. After reaching reproductive maturity, adults mate, and females lay further eggs on host plants, repeating the life cycle.

tasks.title: The Mosquito Life Cycle
tasks.sourceLabel: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
tasks.prompt: The diagram illustrates the main stages in the life cycle of a mosquito, from egg to reproducing adult.
stages: A female mosquito deposits eggs on or near water.
Suitable water conditions trigger the eggs to hatch.
The larvae live and feed in water.
The larvae develop into aquatic pupae.
Winged adults emerge from the pupal stage.
Adult females reproduce and deposit another batch of eggs.
tasks.overview: Overall, mosquitoes undergo a repeating seven-stage life cycle with four main forms: egg, larva, pupa and adult. The three immature stages are associated with water, whereas adults fly and reproduce before another batch of eggs is laid.
tasks.body1: The cycle begins when a female mosquito deposits eggs on or near a source of water. Under suitable conditions, the eggs hatch and young larvae enter the water. During this period, the larvae feed and grow. As they develop, they repeatedly moult, shedding their outer covering before entering the next main stage.
tasks.body2: The fully grown larvae transform into pupae, which remain in the water while further changes take place. Winged adult mosquitoes eventually emerge from the pupal cases and leave the water surface. After reaching maturity and mating, female mosquitoes can lay a new set of eggs, allowing the entire sequence to begin again.

tasks.title: The Sea Turtle Life Cycle
tasks.sourceLabel: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration
tasks.prompt: The diagram shows a simplified sea turtle life cycle, from eggs on a nesting beach to mature turtles that return to reproduce.
stages: An adult female lays eggs in a sandy beach nest.
Embryos develop inside buried eggs before hatching.
Small hatchlings move across the beach and enter the sea.
Young turtles grow in offshore ocean habitats.
Larger juveniles feed and continue growing near coastal waters.
Mature turtles migrate and mate in breeding areas.
Mature females return to nesting beaches and lay eggs.
tasks.overview: Overall, the sea turtle's life cycle passes through seven main stages, beginning with eggs laid on a beach and ending when mature females return to nest again. Development takes place first on land and then across several marine habitats before reproduction.
tasks.body1: The process starts when a mature female sea turtle comes ashore and lays a clutch of eggs in a sandy nest. The embryos develop within the buried eggs, and hatchlings eventually emerge. These small turtles make their way across the beach to the sea, where they enter an oceanic phase and begin growing in offshore habitats.
tasks.body2: As they increase in size, young sea turtles gradually move through juvenile stages and may feed in coastal waters. Once they reach adulthood, they undertake migrations between feeding and breeding areas and mate. Finally, mature females return to nesting beaches to deposit eggs, thereby beginning the next generation and completing the cycle.
